# A sum of two limbs rounded up

Kernel `add_up_1` · **UNVERIFIED** for finite operands · **UNVERIFIED** for infinite and NaN operands · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

**UNVERIFIED: no proof is checked.** The statement below is a target: Rocq has not checked a proof of it. No public operation calls it yet ([What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#proved-and-unverified)).

## What it computes

$a + b$ rounded to a number of `T`:

$$r = \mathrm{RU}(a + b).$$

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of [`add_up_entry`](add_up_entry.md), [`sub_up_1`](sub_up_1.md).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.

## Target (not proved)

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $r = \mathrm{RU}(a + b)$: the smallest number of the format not below $a + b$.

Stated for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**UNVERIFIED.** No proof of the statement is checked.

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition add_up_1_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (2 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall a b : R,
  fmt emin prec a ->
  fmt emin prec b ->
  let r := add_up_1 emin prec tie_even a b in
  fmt emin prec r /\
  r = RU emin prec (a + b).
```

## Infinite and NaN operands

The statement above is about finite operands. The claims also say what the kernel returns when its operands may be infinite or NaN. That statement requires:

- $a$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.
- $b$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.

and then:

- If every operand is finite: $r$ is the smallest number of `T` not below $a + b$, or $+\infty$ when $a + b > \Omega$ ($\Omega$ is the largest finite number of `T`).
- If an operand is infinite or NaN: $r = a + b$, as `T` computes it.

Stated for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

**Status of this statement: UNVERIFIED.** No proof of it is checked (`ieee_status` is `unverified` in `gen/claims.json`). The [Proofs](../proofs/index.md#what-is-proved-and-in-which-model) page says which statements of the IEEE model are proved against statements written by hand; this page gives the status that `gen/claims.json` gives.

## Source

**Algorithm:** the rounded sum and the sign of its exact error (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/add_up_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/add_up_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`two_sum_ord`](two_sum_ord.md).

```
# RU(a + b), the smallest number of the format not below the exact sum, for every pair of finite
# numbers (milestone2.md, "Rounding a sum down and up"): the rounded sum, one step up when its
# exact error is positive. At an overflow the error term is the infinity of the opposite sign:
# +inf for a sum that overflows upward, -Omega for one that overflows downward (the format with
# overflow). An infinite or NaN operand gives the sum of IEEE 754.

(s, e) = two_sum_ord(a, b)
n      = lt(0, e)
q      = succ(s)
r      = select(n, q, s)
```
